geo_headlines: OIL BOUNCES AFTER AN 8% DROP. **January Brent $96.06 (+1.5%) after settling $94.62 Wednesday, down about 8.7% and its lowest since late August, as Gulf sources said a weakened Trump facing a Democratic Congress has more reason to seek a deal (Al Jazeera, Reuters).** The rebound came after the IRGC said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire on unauthorised Hormuz routes and claimed it seized two US drones (Reuters, Trend).

TRUMP: WAR COST US THE ELECTION, WOULD DO IT AGAIN. Trump said it was largely true that the Iran war cost Republicans the midterms by pushing up gasoline, but said he would do it again because Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon (AP, DW). Vance wrote that the reason we lost is the war (BBC). Axios says Trump must now choose between a deal and renewed bombing (Axios).

TEHRAN DIGS IN. The supreme leader said the election changes nothing and US hostility will persist; Iran says it has a maximum deterrence plan ready (Al Jazeera, Daily Star). A tanker was hit by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Qatar (UKMTO via CBS). The US sanctioned Indian and Turkish firms over Iranian oil (Al Jazeera).

FUTURES MIXED AFTER A BIG RALLY. S&P 500 futures 7,727.25 (+0.1%), Nasdaq 100 futures 28,423.75 (-0.5%) as AI names extend losses: Micron and Sandisk fell 7-8% Wednesday and slid again overnight (Benzinga). Gold $4,137.10 (+1.6%). Bitcoin $80,213.

WEDNESDAY: DOW'S BEST DAY OF 2026. Dow +3.03% to 53,356.12, S&P 500 +1.58% to 7,688.62 (1.67% below its October 6 record close), Nasdaq Composite +1.44%; chips -3.1%. VIX fell to 16.61 (Yahoo Finance, Polygon).

TODAY. Bank of England decision 7:00 AM ET, widely expected to raise Bank Rate to 4.00% from 3.75% (Bank of England, AOL). Jobless claims and Q3 productivity 8:30 AM. Friday: October payrolls 8:30 AM.
client_frame_short: The market's verdict on the election came fast: the Dow had its best day of the year, the S&P 500 rose 1.6% and oil fell about 8% on hopes that a weakened White House will now seek a deal with Iran. **Overnight the picture is more mixed: oil is bouncing on new tanker fires, Iran says the vote changes nothing, and AI chip stocks are sliding on fears of tighter rules under a Democratic Congress.** For clients: this is rotation, not panic, and the jobs report lands tomorrow. Stay diversified and rebalance toward targets.
client_frame:
If a client calls this morning, the short version is that the election sparked a broad relief rally, but the leadership underneath is changing.

What happened: Wednesday the Dow jumped 3%, its best day of 2026, and the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to about 1.7% below its October 6 record close. Oil fell about 8%, with Brent near $95, as investors bet that a Democratic Congress makes a negotiated end to the Iran war more likely. Volatility dropped sharply, with the VIX at 16.6. At the same time, chip stocks fell about 3% as investors worried about tighter rules for AI data centers.

What changed overnight: oil bounced about 1.5% after Iran said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said the war largely cost Republicans the election but that he would do it again, and Iran's supreme leader said the vote changes nothing. Stock futures are mixed, with the Nasdaq 100 down 0.5%.

Where we stand: the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.90%. Futures markets now see an 83% chance of a December Fed hike, and the Bank of England is expected to raise rates this morning. The October jobs report comes tomorrow.

Why it matters: lower oil is helping, but central banks are still leaning toward tightening, and the market is rotating away from the most crowded AI names toward a broader set of companies. That favors diversified portfolios over concentrated tech bets. Divided government also tends to mean fewer surprise policy changes, which markets have usually welcomed over time.

For clients: stay invested, rebalance toward targets, and avoid chasing Wednesday's rally or selling into the AI pullback. What would change the view: a 10-year close above 5.40% (Wednesday 4.90%), a 30-year above 5.75% (Wednesday 5.28%), or renewed US strikes that send Brent back well above $105 (now $96.06).
